title: A Blood Vessel Clue in Pregnancy Blood Pressure
paragraphs: Preeclampsia is a serious problem in pregnancy. The mother's blood pressure becomes high. It affects between 2% and 8% of pregnancies around the world. Today, the only real cure is to deliver the baby.

Scientists at the University of Manchester studied tiny blood vessels from pregnant women, with and without preeclampsia. They found that a calcium signal, called a calcium spark, was weaker in women with preeclampsia. It was lower by up to 75%.

This signal helps the vessels relax. The scientists also tested a small protein called HBD2. It did not repair the signal, but it still helped the vessels relax in another way. More research is needed before there is any new medicine.
